questions.questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'She studied hard, ___ she passed the examination.'
questions.explanation: So shows the result of studying hard.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, pupils.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to state or identify something exactly.

questions.questionText: Which register is most appropriate for a formal letter to a school head?
questions.explanation: A formal letter requires respectful, appropriate language.

questions.questionText: Which reading skill involves looking quickly for a specific date or name?
questions.explanation: Scanning is used to locate specific information quickly.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: A direct quotation is separated from the reporting clause with appropriate punctuation.

questions.questionText: Which word is a synonym for 'diligent'?
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a metaphor?
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly describes one thing as another.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a report?
questions.explanation: Reports present organised information, often based on observations or findings.

questions.questionText: Which opening is most appropriate for a formal complaint letter?
questions.explanation: The first option uses an appropriate formal register.

questions.questionText: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'reluctant'.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.questionText: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'scarce'.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; abundant is the opposite.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: The plural possessive girls' indicates books belonging to more than one girl.

questions.questionText: Which word is an adjective in the sentence 'The narrow road was flooded'?
questions.explanation: Narrow describes the noun road.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
questions.explanation: The subject receives the action in the passive construction.

questions.questionText:
**Passage:**
Every morning before sunrise, Nyasha walked three kilometres along the dusty footpath to Nyanga Secondary School, carrying her battered canvas satchel. Despite power cuts at home that forced her to revise by solar lantern, she topped Form 3 in Chemistry and English. Her teacher noticed her quiet persistence and nominated her for the district science Olympiad.

(a) Give two challenges Nyasha faced while preparing for school. [2 marks]
(b) What evidence shows that Nyasha was academically successful? [1 mark]
(c) Explain in your own words the meaning of "quiet persistence". [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Walking 3 km every morning before sunrise along a dusty path; studying under frequent home power cuts using a solar lantern [2 marks].
(b) She came first in Form 3 Chemistry and English [1 mark].
(c) Determined, steady hard work carried out calmly without boasting or complaining [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
**Passage:**
Smallholder irrigation schemes along the Save Valley have transformed formerly drought-prone villages. By replacing open earthen canals—where up to half the water evaporated or seeped away—with lined drip pipes, farmers now harvest green maize and tomatoes twice a year. Youth cooperatives manage pump maintenance and sell surplus produce directly to Mutare markets.

Summary Task (Max 60 words): Summarise the benefits brought by the new irrigation practices to the Save Valley communities. [10 marks]
questions.explanation: Key summary points (2 marks each for any 5 clear points, continuous prose within word limit): 1. Villages previously vulnerable to drought are transformed. 2. Lined drip pipes stop water loss from evaporation and seepage. 3. Farmers harvest maize and tomatoes twice annually. 4. Youth cooperatives gain technical skills maintaining pumps. 5. Surplus crops sold in Mutare boost household incomes. [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Section A Composition (350–450 words): Write a discursive essay titled: "Social media does more harm than good to O-Level students." Discuss both sides before stating your justified conclusion. [30 marks]
questions.explanation: Mark Scheme: Balanced arguments FOR harm (screen addiction, sleep loss, cyberbullying, misinformation/distraction from revision) [10]; Arguments AGAINST / benefits (educational videos, peer study groups, quick access to past papers/digital libraries) [10]; Clear personal conclusion, logical paragraph linking, varied vocabulary & accurate grammar [10]. Total: [30 marks].

questions.questionText: Section B Guided Writing (Speech): As Senior Prefect, write a speech to be delivered at a Parents' Consultation Day proposing three practical ways parents and teachers can curb substance abuse among teenagers. [20 marks]
questions.explanation: Mark Scheme: Appropriate speech greeting & audience engagement [3]; Three concrete proposals well developed (e.g., open parent-teen dialogue, random school bag checks & counselling support, funding after-school sports/clubs) [12]; Persuasive rhetorical tone, clear paragraphing & grammatical accuracy [5]. Total: [20 marks].

questions.questionText: Section B Guided Writing (Formal Report): Following a fire scare in the school laboratory, write an official report to the Headmaster detailing what happened, the cause, and four safety recommendations. [20 marks]
questions.explanation: Mark Scheme: Report format (TO, FROM, DATE, SUBJECT) [3]; Objective chronological account & clear root cause (e.g., unattended Bunsen burner near ethanol bottle) [7]; Four actionable recommendations (fire extinguishers serviced, safety briefing, locked chemical store, emergency drill) [6]; Formal impersonal register & accuracy [4]. Total: [20 marks].

questions.questionText: Section A Narrative Composition (350–450 words): Write a story ending with the words: "...Looking back at the charred ruins, I realised how costly a single moment of carelessness had been." [30 marks]
questions.explanation: Mark Scheme: Smooth realistic plot build-up leading credibly to a fire/accident caused by carelessness [14]; Vivid sensory description, suspense, and emotional reflection [8]; Seamless ending with the exact required sentence and clean mechanics [8]. Total: [30 marks].

questions.questionText: Section B Formal Letter: You noticed broken streetlights and uncollected refuse along your suburb's main road. Write a letter to the Town Clerk urging council action and proposing community support. [20 marks]
questions.explanation: Mark Scheme: Two formal addresses, date, Dear Sir/Madam, underlined heading [4]; Clear explanation of safety & health hazards (night crime, disease vectors) + constructive offer of residents' clean-up partnership [11]; Polite firm tone & Yours faithfully close [5]. Total: [20 marks].

questions.questionText:
Grammar & Register Editing: Rewrite the following faulty sentences correctly:
(a) "Myself and Tendai we went to Bulawayo yesterday." [2 marks]
(b) "The teacher insisted that everyone must bring their own calculator." (Keep formal concord) [2 marks]
(c) "Being a rainy day, the match was cancelled." (Fix dangling participle) [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Tendai and I went to Bulawayo yesterday [2 marks].
(b) The teacher insisted that everyone bring his or her own calculator [2 marks].
(c) Since it was a rainy day, the match was cancelled [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Register & Tone Exercise: Explain why the reply "Shut up and wait outside!" is inappropriate when spoken by a hospital receptionist to an elderly patient, and rewrite it politely in appropriate register. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: It is rude, aggressive, disrespectful toward an elder, and violates professional healthcare empathy/Ubuntu [2 marks]. Polite alternative: "Good morning, Gogo/Sekuru. Kindly take a seat in the waiting area and the nurse will call you shortly." [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Vocabulary in Context: Read: "Although the committee's initial proposal met stiff resistance, the chairperson's tactful compromises gradually placated even the sharpest critics."
Explain the meanings of (a) "stiff resistance", (b) "tactful", and (c) "placated". [6 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Strong, determined opposition [2 marks]. (b) Sensitive, diplomatic, avoiding giving unnecessary offence [2 marks]. (c) Calmed down or satisfied angry critics [2 marks].
